mainTopic: The mourning period before תשעה באב, the restrictions on the last meal before the fast, and the laws of an אבל on תשעה באב itself.
overview: This amud opens by showing how three opinions about the mourning period before תשעה באב each come from a different word in one פסוק. רבא then rules leniently: the restrictions start only in the week of תשעה באב, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, and end at the fast, as רבי מאיר says. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's ban on two cooked dishes on ערב תשעה באב. רב יהודה limits it to the last meal before the fast, eaten after midday, and ברייתות support both limits. More ברייתות show how the תנאים disagree about meat, wine and bathing at that meal. A ברייתא then teaches that on תשעה באב itself all the laws of an אבל apply, including a ban on לימוד תורה, with exceptions for sad material. The גמרא defines which salted meat and new wine are still allowed at the last meal. It closes by starting a story about the very strict practice of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Each opinion learns its time period from a different word in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes showing how each תנא draws his opinion from the פסוק 'וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי כׇּל מְשׂוֹשָׂהּ חַגָּהּ חׇדְשָׁהּ וְשַׁבַּתָּהּ.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [The one who said the restrictions start from ראש חודש learns it] from 'her festival.' The one who said the whole month is forbidden learns it from 'her new moon.' The one who said only that whole week is forbidden learns it from 'her Shabbat.'
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins mid-sentence. The גמרא is linking each of three opinions about the mourning period to a different word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the restrictions run from ראש חודש until the fast. He learns this from 'חַגָּהּ,' because ראש חודש is treated like a kind of festival. רבי יהודה says the whole month, from 'חׇדְשָׁהּ' (her month). רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says only the week of תשעה באב, from 'שַׁבַּתָּהּ,' which can also mean a week.

keyTerms.meaning: Her festival. Here it refers to ראש חודש.
Her Shabbat. Here it means the week.

steps.confusionAlert: The first word, 'מֵחַגָּה,' completes a sentence from the previous עמוד. The missing first half is: 'the one who said from ראש חודש until the fast (רבי מאיר) learns it...'

phrases.english: [learns it] from 'her festival.'
phrases.notes: The opinion of רבי מאיר: from ראש חודש until the fast.

phrases.english: And the one who said the whole [month] is forbidden — from 'her new moon,'

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר כׇּל הַשַּׁבָּת כּוּלָּהּ אָסוּר — מִ״שַּׁבַּתָּהּ״.
phrases.english: and the one who said the entire week is forbidden — from 'her Shabbat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a derivation that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three opinions come from one פסוק. Each focuses on a different word: חגה = from ראש חודש, חדשה = the whole month, שבתה = the week.

steps.title: רבא rules like two opinions, both leniently
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and also like רבי מאיר. Both rulings are meant to be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. And רבא also said: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר. Both rulings are meant as leniencies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the practical ruling. He follows two different opinions, each on the point where that opinion is more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree about when the restrictions start and when they end. רבא takes the lenient side of each. The start follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: only the week of תשעה באב, not from ראש חודש. The end follows רבי מאיר: only until the fast, not after it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line: the restrictions apply in the week of תשעה באב, and only until the fast itself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
And Rava said: The halacha follows Rabbi Meir.
And both of them are for leniency,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling among the opinions that were just derived.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on the start (only that week) and רבי מאיר on the end (only until the fast).

steps.title: Why the ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a ruling like רבי מאיר alone would have suggested the restrictions begin at ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both rulings are needed. If רבא had only taught that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר, I would have thought the restrictions start even from ראש חודש. So he teaches that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why did רבא need two rulings? This step explains the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is lenient about the end, but he is strict about the start (from ראש חודש). A ruling like רבי מאיר alone might seem to accept his whole view, including the early start. The ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל shows that the start is only the week of תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to state both)

phrases.english: And it is necessary.
For if he had taught us 'the halacha follows Rabbi Meir,'
I would have said: even from Rosh Chodesh,

phrases.aramaic: קָמַשְׁמַע לַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: so he teaches us the halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the first of רבא's two rulings was needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Implied question: why did רבא state two rulings?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without the ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, we would have started the restrictions from ראש חודש, following רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Why the ruling like רבי מאיר was needed
steps.stepSummary: A ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל alone would have suggested the restrictions continue after the fast, through the rest of the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רבא had only taught that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, I would have thought the restrictions apply even after the fast. So he teaches that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation by showing why the second ruling, like רבי מאיר, was also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids 'that whole week.' That could include the days after תשעה באב. רבי מאיר's phrase 'until the fast' sets the end point. So the restrictions stop once the fast arrives.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא combines two leniencies. The restrictions begin only in the week of תשעה באב, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says. They end at the fast, as רבי מאיר says.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: And if he had taught us 'the halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,'
I would have said: even after it [the fast],
so he teaches us the halacha follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of why both rulings were needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without the ruling like רבי מאיר, we would have extended the restrictions past the fast for the rest of the week.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on two cooked dishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on ערב תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the eve of תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up רב יהודה's explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This quote opens a new section. The משנה limits the meal before the fast to one cooked dish, as a sign of mourning. The next steps will limit when this rule applies.

phrases.english: On the eve of the Ninth of Av

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: a person may not eat two cooked dishes, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב תשעה באב one may not eat two cooked dishes.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the ban applies only after midday
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה limits the משנה's ban to the time from six hours of the day (midday) and onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: They only taught this from six hours [of the day] and later. But before six hours, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה narrows the משנה's rule. The ban on two cooked dishes only starts at midday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says 'ערב תשעה באב,' which could sound like the whole day. רב יהודה limits it to the second half of the day, when the fast is getting close. A meal before midday may include two dishes.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught [this rule] in the case of...

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: They taught this only
from six hours and onward,
but from six hours and earlier — it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits when the משנה's rule applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on two cooked dishes applies only from midday onward.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the ban applies only to the final meal before the fast
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה further limits the ban to the סעודה המפסקת, the last meal before the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: They only taught this about the meal with which one ends eating before the fast. But at a meal that is not the final one, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה adds a second limit. The ban applies only to the last meal before the fast begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after midday, a meal that is not the final one may include two dishes. Only the סעודה המפסקת, eaten right before the fast, is restricted. This is a separate limit from the time limit in the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: The final meal before the fast (סעודה המפסקת)
A meal that is not the final one

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, the ban on two cooked dishes applies only at the final meal (סעודה המפסקת), eaten after midday on ערב תשעה באב.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said: They taught this only
regarding the meal with which one concludes [before the fast],

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּסְעוּדָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַפְסִיק בָּהּ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: but at a meal with which one does not conclude — it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּסְעוּדָה הַמַּפְסִיק בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit, by type of meal, alongside the time limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies only at the סעודה המפסקת. Other meals may include two cooked dishes.

steps.title: Both limits are leniencies, and the 'six hours' limit is needed
steps.stepSummary: Both of רב יהודה's statements make the law easier. If he had only said 'the last meal,' we might think even a morning last meal is restricted, so he also said 'from six hours onward.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Both statements are meant to make things easier, and we need both. If he had only told us 'the meal by which he stops,' I would have thought it applies even before midday. So he teaches us: only from six hours onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב יהודה's two limits do not repeat each other. Here it explains why the 'six hours' limit is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each limit cuts down the ban in a different way. 'Last meal' alone would still forbid a final meal eaten in the morning. The 'six hours' limit tells us a morning meal is allowed even if it is the last one.

keyTerms.meaning: For leniency; to make the law easier
And it is necessary to state both
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one of רב יהודה's limits makes the law stricter. Both of them shrink the ban. The ban applies only when BOTH conditions are true: it is after midday AND it is the last meal before the fast.

phrases.english: And both of them are for leniency,
and it is necessary to state both.
For if he had taught us only 'at the meal by which he stops [before the fast],'

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אֲפִילּוּ מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּלְמַטָּה —
phrases.english: I would have said: even from six hours and earlier.
So he teaches us: only from six hours and onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב יהודה needed both of the limits given in steps 6 and 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'six hours' limit is needed so we know that a last meal eaten before midday is allowed

steps.title: Why the 'last meal' limit is also needed
steps.stepSummary: If רב יהודה had only said 'from six hours onward,' we might think every afternoon meal is restricted. So he also said 'only the last meal.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only told us 'from six hours onward,' I would have thought it applies even to a meal that is not the last one. So he teaches us: only the meal by which he stops.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the 'both are needed' argument. It shows why the 'last meal' limit is also necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'six hours' limit alone would still forbid an afternoon meal that is not the final one. The 'last meal' limit tells us such a meal is allowed. Each limit removes a case the other one would have left forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal that is not the last one before the fast
The final meal before the fast begins

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on two cooked dishes applies only to the last meal before the fast, and only when it is eaten after midday.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only 'from six hours and onward,'

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אֲפִילּוּ בִּסְעוּדָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַפְסִיק בָּהּ —
phrases.english: I would have said: even at a meal by which he does not stop [before the fast].
So he teaches us: only at the meal by which he stops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the explanation of why both limits are needed
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'last meal' limit is needed so we know that an afternoon meal that is not the last one is allowed

steps.title: Both versions have support from ברייתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that a ברייתא supports the first version and another supports the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like the first version. It was taught in a ברייתא like the second version.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that it is about to bring a supporting ברייתא for each version, and the next steps quote them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'first version' is the 'six hours' limit, and the 'second version' is the 'last meal' limit. Neither one is just רב יהודה's own idea; each matches a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita like the first version.
It was taught in a baraita like the second version.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא. תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the two limits, the גמרא now announces support for each
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות, quoted in the next steps

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting the 'last meal' version
steps.stepSummary: If a person will eat another meal later, he may have meat and wine now. If this is his last meal, he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught like the second version: One who eats a meal on ערב תשעה באב: if he plans to eat another meal later, he may eat meat and drink wine. If not, he may not eat meat or drink wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that supports the 'last meal' limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the restriction depend on whether another meal is coming. That is exactly the 'last meal' idea: only the final meal before the fast is restricted.

phrases.english: It was taught like the second version:
One who eats a meal on the eve of the Ninth of Av,
if he plans to eat another meal,
he is permitted to eat meat and drink wine;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אָסוּר לֶאֱכוֹל בָּשָׂר וְלִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן.
phrases.english: and if not, he is forbidden to eat meat and drink wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the first of the two promised ברייתות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that makes the ban depend on whether another meal will follow

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting the 'six hours' version: the basic ban
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that on ערב תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes, meat, or wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he should just change his normal eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught like the first version: On ערב תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes, and may not eat meat or drink wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he should change [his usual habits].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא that supports the 'six hours' limit. This part gives the basic ban, and the supporting line comes at the end (step 14).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives a full ban on two dishes, meat and wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is gentler: a person does not have to stop entirely, only change from his usual way of eating.

phrases.english: It was taught like the first version:
On the eve of the Ninth of Av
a person may not eat two cooked dishes;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן.
phrases.english: he may not eat meat and may not drink wine.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: יְשַׁנֶּה.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: he should change [his habits].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the second promised ברייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא whose closing clause limits the ban to after six hours

steps.title: רבי יהודה explains how to change one's habits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives examples of cutting back: one dish instead of two, eating with five people instead of ten, drinking five cups instead of ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: How does he change? If he usually eats two cooked dishes, he should eat one kind. If he usually eats with ten people, he eats with five. If he usually drinks ten cups, he drinks five cups.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי יהודה explains what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'change' looks like in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Change' means cutting back noticeably compared to what the person normally does. It is measured against his own usual habit, not one fixed amount for everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: This רבי יהודה is the תנא quoted in the ברייתא. He is not רב יהודה, the אמורא of steps 6–7.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: How does he change?

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה רָגִיל לֶאֱכוֹל שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין —
phrases.english: If he was used to eating two cooked dishes,
he should eat one kind;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיָה רָגִיל לִסְעוֹד בַּעֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם —
phrases.english: and if he was used to dining with ten people,
he dines with five;
if he was used to drinking ten cups,
he drinks five cups.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word יְשַׁנֶּה from step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Changing means cutting down noticeably from one's normal habit

steps.title: The ban applies only from six hours onward
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying all of this applies only after midday. Before midday everything is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? From six hours and onward. But from six hours and earlier, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line of the ברייתא that actually supports the first version, the 'six hours' limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא itself limits the restrictions to the afternoon, exactly as רב יהודה's first version said. This is why the גמרא called it a ברייתא 'like the first version.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This clause is the actual proof for the 'six hours' limit. The rest of the ברייתא only provides background.

phrases.english: When are these words said?
From six hours and onward;
but from six hours and earlier, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the clause that proves the first version
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The restrictions apply only after midday

steps.title: Another ברייתא: רבי מאיר forbids, חכמים say cut back
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר forbids two dishes, meat, and wine on ערב תשעה באב. חכמים say a person should change his habits and eat less meat and drink less wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: On ערב תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes, and may not eat meat or drink wine. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: he should change, and eat less meat and drink less wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא that presents the same topic as an argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the full ban is said in the name of רבי מאיר. חכמים do not forbid meat and wine completely; they only require a person to have less of them.

phrases.english: Another baraita teaches:

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין,
phrases.english: On the eve of the Ninth of Av a person may not eat two cooked dishes;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן,
phrases.english: he may not eat meat and may not drink wine;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: he should change [his habits],
and reduce the meat and the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that shows a dispute about the same rules
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר gives a full ban; חכמים require only cutting down on meat and wine

steps.title: How much to cut back on meat and wine
steps.stepSummary: Someone who usually eats a ליטרא of meat eats half. Someone who usually drinks a לוג of wine drinks half. Someone who normally has none may have none.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he reduce? If he usually eats a ליטרא of meat, he eats half a ליטרא. If he usually drinks a לוג of wine, he drinks half a לוג. And if he is not used to them at all, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the חכמים's 'cutting back' with clear amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount is half of what the person normally has. Someone who never normally eats meat or drinks wine may not start on ערב תשעה באב, since there is nothing to cut back from.

keyTerms.meaning: A ליטרא, a unit of weight

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not used to it at all' does not mean he is let off the rule. It means he may not have meat or wine at all on this day.

phrases.english: How does he reduce?

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה רָגִיל לֶאֱכוֹל לִיטְרָא בָּשָׂר —
phrases.english: If he was used to eating a litra of meat,
he should eat half a litra;
if he was used to drinking a log of wine,
he should drink half a log of wine;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ רָגִיל כׇּל עִיקָּר — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: and if he is not used to them at all, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the חכמים's word מְמַעֵט from step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reduce to half of one's usual amount; someone with no usual amount may have none

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a usual radish or salted food
steps.stepSummary: If a person normally eats a radish or a salted food after his meal, he may do so on ערב תשעה באב too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If he usually eats a radish or a salted food after his meal, he is allowed to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a lenient point: a small usual side food after the meal is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A radish or salted food eaten after the meal does not count as a second cooked dish. So a person may keep this habit even at the last meal before the fast.

keyTerms.meaning: A salted food (such as salted fish)
He is allowed; it is up to him

steps.whatToRemember: On ערב תשעה באב the restrictions apply only to the last meal, and only after midday (רב יהודה). The תנאים disagree on how strict they are: רבי מאיר gives a full ban, חכמים say to cut back to half, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a usual radish or salted food.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה רָגִיל לֶאֱכוֹל צְנוֹן אוֹ מָלִיחַ אַחַר סְעוּדָּתוֹ —
phrases.english: If he was used to eating a radish or a salted food after his meal,
he has permission [to do so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the same ברייתא, adding a leniency
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A usual radish or salted food after the meal is allowed on ערב תשעה באב

steps.title: Another ברייתא: Meat, Wine and Bathing Before the Fast
steps.stepSummary: A meal eaten because of תשעה באב may not have meat or wine, and bathing is forbidden. A meal not connected to תשעה באב may have meat and wine, but bathing is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: In any meal that is because of תשעה באב, it is forbidden to eat meat, forbidden to drink wine, and forbidden to bathe. In any meal that is not because of תשעה באב, it is permitted to eat meat and drink wine, but it is forbidden to bathe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about the meal before the fast. It divides meals into two kinds: a meal eaten because of תשעה באב, and a meal that is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meal eaten 'because of' the fast is the final meal before it, the סעודה המפסקת. Only that meal gets the full restrictions on meat and wine. A meal that is not tied to the fast may have meat and wine. However, this ברייתא still forbids bathing in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of תשעה באב, meaning the meal eaten in preparation for the fast
The final meal before a fast (not in the text, but this is what the ברייתא is talking about)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that bathing is forbidden in BOTH cases, even when meat and wine are allowed. That is exactly the point רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי will challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
Any meal that is because of the Ninth of Av —
phrases.notes: The final meal before the fast

phrases.english: it is forbidden to eat meat
and forbidden to drink wine
and forbidden to bathe.
Any meal that is not because of the Ninth of Av —
it is permitted to eat meat and drink wine
but forbidden to bathe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ברייתא on the meal before the fast, after the earlier steps on cutting back meat and wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the meal tied to the fast: no meat, no wine, no bathing. In a meal not tied to the fast: meat and wine are allowed, but bathing is still forbidden.

steps.title: Bathing Follows Meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, quoting his father, says that whenever meat is allowed, bathing is allowed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי says in the name of his father: Any time that one is permitted to eat meat, one is permitted to bathe.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion inside the same ברייתא disagrees with the last clause. It argues that bathing should follow the same rule as meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion forbade bathing even when meat was allowed. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי links the two rules together. So in a meal not tied to the fast, where meat is allowed, bathing is allowed as well.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוסי
In the name of his father

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei says in the name of his father:
Any time that one is permitted to eat meat —
one is permitted to bathe.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's ban on bathing in a meal not tied to the fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bathing is permitted whenever eating meat is permitted.

steps.title: תשעה באב Has the Laws of an אבל
steps.stepSummary: Everything an אבל keeps also applies on תשעה באב. That means no eating, drinking, anointing, leather shoes or marital relations, and no learning any part of תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: All the laws practiced by an אבל are practiced on תשעה באב. It is forbidden to eat, drink, anoint oneself, wear shoes, or have marital relations. It is forbidden to read the תורה, the נביאים and the כתובים, and to learn משנה, תלמוד, מדרש, הלכות and אגדות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from the day before to תשעה באב itself. It brings a ברייתא that compares the day to a mourner's practices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that whatever an אבל may not do, a person on תשעה באב may not do. Five physical comforts are banned. לימוד תורה is also banned, because תורה brings joy, as the next step will show from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: To learn or review Oral Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the basis for treating תשעה באב like a day of mourning. Its physical restrictions (eating and drinking, anointing, shoes, marital relations) and the ban on לימוד תורה all follow from the laws of an אבל.
steps.confusionAlert: לימוד תורה is not banned because it is a bad thing. It is banned because it makes a person happy, and תשעה באב is a day of mourning.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All the laws practiced by a mourner —
are practiced on the Ninth of Av;
it is forbidden to eat, to drink, to anoint oneself,
to wear shoes, and to have marital relations.
And it is forbidden to read the Torah, the Prophets and the Writings,
or to learn Mishnah, Talmud and Midrash
and halachot and aggadot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל מִצְוֹת הַנּוֹהֲגוֹת בְּאָבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meal before the fast to the laws of the fast day itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the restrictions of an אבל apply on תשעה באב, including the five physical prohibitions and the ban on לימוד תורה.

steps.title: What One May Still Learn on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: One may learn material he is not used to learning, plus איכה, איוב and the harsh prophecies of ירמיה. Schoolchildren stop learning, because תורה gladdens the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a person may read a part of תנ״ך he is not used to reading, and learn a part he is not used to learning. He may read איכה, איוב, and the bad prophecies in ירמיה. Schoolchildren stop learning, because it says: 'The commands of ה׳ are upright, gladdening the heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives exceptions to the ban on learning. It then explains, from a פסוק, why learning is banned at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unfamiliar material is hard, so it does not give the usual pleasure. Sad books like איכה, איוב and ירמיה's warnings fit the mood of mourning. The פסוק 'משמחי לב' explains the whole rule: תורה brings joy, so even young children take the day off.

keyTerms.meaning: That he is not used to (learning)

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קוֹרֵא הוּא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָגִיל לִקְרוֹת,
phrases.english: But he may read in a place he is not used to reading,
and learn in a place he is not used to learning,
and he may read Lamentations and Job,
and the harsh prophecies in Jeremiah.
And schoolchildren stop learning,
because it is said:
"The precepts of the Lord are right, gladdening the heart" (Psalms 19:9).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל קוֹרֵא הוּא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָגִיל לִקְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists exceptions to the ban on Torah study and gives the פסוק behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfamiliar material and sad material (איכה, איוב, ירמיה) are allowed. Children stop learning because Torah brings joy.

steps.title: רבי יהודה Forbids Even Unfamiliar Learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says one may not learn even unfamiliar material. Only איוב, איכה and the harsh parts of ירמיה are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: A person may not even read a part he is not used to reading, nor learn a part he is not used to learning. But he may read איוב, איכה and the bad prophecies in ירמיהו. And schoolchildren stop learning on that day, because it says: 'The commands of ה׳ are upright, gladdening the heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion on one point. He removes the 'unfamiliar material' exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that sad books are allowed and that children stop learning. They argue only about unfamiliar material. The first opinion says it gives no joy, but רבי יהודה holds that any regular לימוד תורה still brings joy, so he forbids it.
steps.whatToRemember: On תשעה באב, all the restrictions of an אבל apply, including no לימוד תורה, because תורה brings joy. Sad material such as איכה, איוב and ירמיה's warnings is allowed. The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה argue only about unfamiliar material.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָגִיל לִקְרוֹת,
phrases.english: He may not even read in a place he is not used to reading,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹנֶה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָגִיל לִשְׁנוֹת.
phrases.english: nor learn in a place he is not used to learning.
But he may read Job and Lamentations
and the harsh prophecies in Jeremiah.

phrases.aramaic: וְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן בְּטֵלִים בּוֹ,
phrases.english: And schoolchildren stop learning on that day,
because it is said:
"The precepts of the Lord are right, gladdening the heart."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף אֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the first opinion's 'unfamiliar material' exception and agrees with the rest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even unfamiliar material is forbidden. Only sad books are permitted, and children stop learning.

steps.title: Salted meat and new wine are allowed at the last meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on meat and wine before תשעה באב. A ברייתא then allows salted meat and wine fresh from the press.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he may not eat meat or drink wine. A ברייתא taught: but he may eat salted meat and drink wine fresh from his winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on meat and wine at the last meal before תשעה באב. It then brings a ברייתא that carves out two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salted meat and freshly pressed wine do not bring the same joy as regular meat and wine. So they do not break the mournful mood of the meal. This sets up the next questions: exactly what counts as 'salted' and what counts as 'from the press'?

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught (an outside teaching from the time of the משנה)
Wine straight from his winepress, not yet finished fermenting

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן.
phrases.english: He may not eat meat and may not drink wine.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה about the last meal before תשעה באב

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: אֲבָל אוֹכֵל הוּא בָּשָׂר מָלִיחַ
phrases.english: A tanna taught: but he may eat salted meat
and drink wine from his winepress.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֲבָל אוֹכֵל הוּא בָּשָׂר מָלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a new line of the משנה (the meat and wine ban) after the discussion of Torah study on תשעה באב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salted meat and wine fresh from the press are allowed at the last meal before תשעה באב.

steps.title: How long until meat counts as salted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long meat must sit in salt before it counts as 'salted meat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Salted meat: how long must it be salted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא's first exception. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat salted for only a moment is still ordinary meat. So there must be a minimum time before it changes status, and the גמרא wants that time.

keyTerms.meaning: How long? (asking for a time limit)

phrases.english: Salted meat, how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term from the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum salting time needed for meat to count as 'salted meat'

steps.title: שמואל: as long as it is within the time limit of שלמים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that while the meat is within the eating time of שלמים, it is still regular meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר כהנא said in the name of שמואל: as long as it is like שלמים, it is still considered meat.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the time limit. Meat is still 'real meat' for as long as שלמים may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים may be eaten for two days and the night between them. During that window, meat is still treated as fresh meat. Only meat salted for longer than that counts as 'salted meat' and is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offerings, which may be eaten for two days and one night

steps.confusionAlert: 'As long as it is like שלמים' describes when the meat is still FORBIDDEN, not when it is allowed. Only after the שלמים window passes does it become permitted salted meat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chinnana bar Kahana said in the name of Shmuel:
As long as it is like peace-offerings.
phrases.notes: Within that time it still counts as meat

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Meat is ordinary meat for the eating time of שלמים (two days and one night). Salted longer than that, it counts as salted meat and is permitted.

steps.title: How long does wine count as fresh from the press?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for how long wine still counts as 'from the press.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And wine from his press: how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the second exception, the new wine. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the question is the reverse. It asks how long the wine stays in its permitted 'new' state before it becomes real wine.

phrases.english: And wine from his press, how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question about the second term in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long wine still counts as 'from the press'

steps.title: As long as it is still fermenting
steps.stepSummary: Wine counts as 'from the press' as long as it is still bubbling and fermenting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as it is fermenting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wine counts as fresh while it is still fermenting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine that is still fermenting is not yet finished, enjoyable wine. So it does not bring joy and is allowed. The exact length of fermentation comes in the next step.

phrases.english: As long as it is fermenting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wine counts as 'from the press,' and is permitted, while it is still fermenting.

steps.title: Fermentation lasts three days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that fermenting wine is not subject to the danger of uncovered liquids, and that fermentation lasts three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: fermenting wine has no problem of being left uncovered. And how long does it ferment? Three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from a different topic, uncovered drinks. It uses the ברייתא to show how long fermentation lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז״ל forbade drinks left uncovered, out of fear a snake drank from them and left venom. Fermenting wine is exempt, because a snake keeps away from it. The ברייתא fixes fermentation at three days, so new wine is allowed for three days after pressing.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids left uncovered, forbidden for fear of snake venom
It does not have the problem of

steps.whatToRemember: At the last meal before תשעה באב: salted meat is allowed only once it is past the שלמים time (two days and one night). New wine is allowed only while it is still fermenting (three days).

phrases.english: A tanna taught: fermenting wine
has no problem of being uncovered,
and how long is its fermenting? Three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: יַיִן תּוֹסֵס אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the exact length of 'fermenting' from step 27
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fermentation lasts three days, so wine is 'from the press' for three days after pressing.

steps.title: The custom of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי before תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: רב describes how רבי יהודה בר אילעאי ate on ערב תשעה באב: they brought him dry bread with salt, and he sat (the story continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: this was the custom of רבי יהודה son of רבי אילעאי. On ערב תשעה באב they would bring him dry bread with salt, and he would sit...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about how one great sage ate his final meal before תשעה באב. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא gave the minimum rules. This story shows a much stricter level of mourning. Instead of salted meat or new wine, the sage ate only dry bread with salt.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַאי:
phrases.english: This was the custom of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Ilai:
On the eve of the Ninth of Av
they would bring him dry bread with salt,
and he would sit
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the technical definitions to a story of a sage's stricter practice at the same meal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בר אילעאי ate only dry bread with salt at his last meal before תשעה באב.
